clue.text: I mostly want to keep seabird captive

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the seabird sits inside the shortened want
mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to want is to need
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone admits they would like to hold a seabird prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captive' looks like an adjective describing the seabird, but it is the definition, as a noun: a person held prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person held in confinement, especially in wartime, is a captive.

clue.text: Symbols badly misread, limiting attempt to rise

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on both sides, so the scrambled letters enclose the attempt
badly misread means read wrongly, so those letters are rearranged
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Signs are badly misread, which holds back an effort to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes IDEARMS; 'to rise' turns the attempt upwards, as befits a down clue, and 'limiting' wraps the scramble around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: characters representing ideas rather than sounds, as in Chinese writing.

clue.text: A lot of shots cornering British people

indicators.note: cornering means trapping, so British is caught inside
a lot of but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: tries are attempts or shots

explanation.surface: A volley of shots hems in British people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' cuts TRIES to TRIE; 'cornering' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tribe is a people or community sharing ancestry and culture.

clue.text: Former Ukrainian in Nauru, then Ecuador

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A displaced Ukrainian lived in Nauru, then Ecuador.
explanation.walkthrough: Nauru is a Pacific island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical term: a Ruthene was a Ruthenian, an older name for a Ukrainian of the western region.

clue.text: Whirlpool's quality implying location of dangerous rocks

parts.note: an eddy is a small whirlpool
tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: The swirl of the water hints at hidden hazards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eddystone rocks, off Plymouth in Devon, carry a famous lighthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: the Eddystone reef in the English Channel is notorious for wrecking ships.

clue.text: Initially carried away in a box

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word carried

parts.note: away means off, as in gone off
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something taken off at the start in a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a coffin is the box in which a body is buried, slangily just a box.

clue.text: American artist accepted rise in price for engravings initially

parts.note: OK means approved or accepted

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, so the price is reversed

parts.note: a fee is a price

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of for and engravings

explanation.surface: An American artist agreed to a price increase for prints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise in' turns FEE into EEF; 'initially' gives FE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Georgia O'Keeffe was an American painter known for flowers and desert landscapes.

clue.text: Golf is man struggling to get birdies?

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Golf finds a man having trouble getting under par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birdies' is golf's one-under-par score; here it is whimsically birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Example with a question mark: flamingos are birds, so playfully called little birds.

clue.text: Looked into request, being pleased with this?

parts.note: take pleased, have ... in it, and what is left is plea, a request

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they will be happy with the result.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: remove S, E, D from PLEASED and PLEA, a request, remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pried or poked about inquisitively.

clue.text: Australian upset over direction of Queensland region

indicators.note: in a down clue over places one piece above the next
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia and Australian
Queensland lies in the north-east of Australia

explanation.surface: An Australian is annoyed about which way Queensland is headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OZ into ZO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an area or district marked off from others.

clue.text: Author rejected reduction in facilities?

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the shortened word is read backwards
a reduction in the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for a lavatory or toilet

explanation.surface: A writer turns down cuts to public amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction in' cuts TOILET to TOILE, which 'rejected' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: George Eliot and T S Eliot are both celebrated writers.

clue.text: More than one bishop is involved with deacons

definitions.note: plural phrase matching a plural noun

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters of is and deacons are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bishop gets mixed up with his deacons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' rearranges IS plus DEACONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan is the bishop in charge of a diocese, so several of them are a group of bishops.

clue.text: Surprised cry encountering wings of some birds

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in surprise at seeing the wings of some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: geese are large waterbirds.

clue.text: German hero is returning, say, suffering from heat

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is is read backwards

parts.note: say introduces an example, as does eg
fried means scorched or overcome by heat

explanation.surface: A German champion comes back home, sweltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Siegfried is the dragon-slaying hero of German legend and of Wagner's Ring cycle.

clue.text: Those people will tuck into ruined toast no more

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, so those people sit within the rearranged toast
ruined toast is spoiled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: Some people are about to eat burnt toast and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' makes ATOST, and 'will tuck into' sets the people inside that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a maximum figure is reached and not exceeded, meaning no more than that.

clue.text: Both sides in soccer match forming a line at Twickenham

definitions.meaning: two teams of eleven players each
Twickenham is England's rugby stadium; the rugby pitch has a line 22 metres from the goal line

explanation.surface: Two football teams line up like a rugby side.
explanation.definitionFit: Number sense: the full complement of players in a soccer game, and a marked line on a rugby field.

clue.text: Sound of horn expert blocked repeatedly by onset of his oral problem

indicators.note: blocked means obstructed, so the letters break into the other pieces

parts.note: toot is the noise a horn makes

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter is used twice
onset means beginning, so the first letter of his

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A horn player is stopped again and again by mouth trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of' gives H and 'repeatedly' makes two; 'blocked' sets them separately, one after the horn's sound and one breaking into the expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pain in a tooth is a common trouble in the mouth.

clue.text: Plant disease, therefore croft's closing

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

indicators.note: the closing letter of croft's is its last before the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A crop blight forces the smallholding to shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing' takes T, the last letter of 'croft'. A croft is a small Scottish farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ergot is a fungal disease of rye and other cereals.

clue.text: Bland or somehow provocative?

definitions.meaning: a joke in poor taste is likely to give offence

explanation.surface: Is a thing dull, or in some way inflammatory?
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: having no flavour, and offending good manners or decency.

clue.text: Space in Puccini opera not leading to dramatic musical item

indicators.note: in places the printers' space inside the shortened opera
not leading with to means the letters to at the front are removed

parts.note: Tosca is an opera by Puccini
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A gap in a Puccini opera fails to produce the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not leading to' strips TO from TOSCA, a neat reading of 'to' as letters, leaving SCA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is an extended dramatic solo passage in opera, a theatrical piece of music.

clue.text: Bill to appear around start of month, forestalling the rot

indicators.note: around tells us the account wraps around the date

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
SEPT 1 is the first day of September, the start of a month

explanation.surface: An invoice arrives at the start of the month, holding off decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of month' is a date, Sept 1, with the figure as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: free from germs, preventing putrefaction or infection.

clue.text: Mix Cross with source of evil, possibly? These do

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter
possibly says these letters could form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to blend the cross with evil, which is what rites of exorcism do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MIX, CROSS and E (the first letter of 'evil', from 'source of'). The definition leans on the rest of the clue: these rites bring cross and evil together.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi-&lit: ceremonies to drive out demons are what bring a cross against evil.

clue.text: Summon corps, at full strength

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for corps, as in military unit names
all out means with maximum effort

explanation.surface: An order to call up the entire army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal-verb synonym: to send for someone or order them to come.

clue.text: Inclined to play King — non-court card is following it — Hearts?

indicators.note: following places the card and is after it

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in cards and chess
a ten is a playing card that is not a court (face) card
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card play

explanation.surface: A card game description: King with a plain card following, in hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: playful like a young cat, so given to frolicking.

clue.text: Gives up exciting activity

definitions.meaning: abandons a habit, as in kicking smoking
thrills, as in doing something for the excitement

explanation.surface: Someone quits thrill-seeking.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: stops a habit, and the thrills sought for fun.

clue.text: A call for attention rising in Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, like a
oi is a shout to get attention

explanation.surface: A shout goes up on a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ANOI upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Landed hard, with little energy, in athletic style

definitions.note: adjectival phrase describing a supple, agile build

parts.note: to land, as a bird does, is to alight; past tense lit
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
E is the abbreviation for energy; little signals the shortening

explanation.surface: An athlete came down heavily, low on energy, yet stylishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: supple and agile, moving gracefully the way an athlete does.

clue.text: Supporter stifling surprised comment and laugh

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the supporter surrounds the comment

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
eh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A fan muffles a shocked remark and a giggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a snigger or titter, a stifled laugh.

clue.text: Whip up action, being transfixed

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, cat for short

indicators.note: up here means stirred up, so the letters of action are mixed

explanation.surface: Stirring someone to action while they are rooted to the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up', as in whipped up, rearranges ACTION to ATONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: in a stupor, rigid and unresponsive, as if frozen in place.

clue.text: Colouring work sees a move for church

indicators.note: a move for these letters means they shift to another position in the word

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Artwork shows a church being relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a move for' shifts CH one place along in CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used for colour.

clue.text: Surprised cry when probing school's heat damage

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so the cry goes inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone gasps while investigating fire damage at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a burn mark left on a surface by heat.

clue.text: Relax — energy will be provided for one in difficulty

indicators.note: provided for means supplied in place of, so one letter swaps for another

parts.note: distress is hardship or difficulty
I is the Roman numeral one
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Advice to unwind: with fresh energy, trouble eases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be provided for' swaps the I in DISTRESS for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to unwind and shed tension, the opposite of becoming anxious.
